overview: Hepatitis A is an inflammation of the liver caused by the hepatitis A virus, primarily spread through contaminated food or water, and can cause mild to severe symptoms. Unlike hepatitis B and C, hepatitis A does not cause chronic liver disease but can cause fulminant hepatitis, which is often fatal. Hepatitis A occurs sporadically and in epidemics worldwide.
diagnosis: detection of HAV-specific immunoglobulin G (IgM) antibodies in the blood
treatment: avoidance of unnecessary medications that can adversely affect the liver
prevention: adequate supplies of safe drinking water
use of condoms, dental dams and good hygiene practices
risk_factors: living in a household with an infected person
being a sexual partner of someone with acute hepatitis A infection
travelling to areas of high endemicity without being immunized
key_facts: 7134 persons died from hepatitis A worldwide in 2016
0.5% of the mortality due to viral hepatitis is caused by hepatitis A
